problem_statement: Programming an emulated MTD device must behave like a NOR flash. After erasing, if a location is programmed twice, the resulting bytes must be the bitwise AND of the two programmed byte sequences; a later program may clear bits but must never set a bit from 0 back to 1. For example, after erasing, mtd_write(dev, [0xEE, 0xDD, 0xCC], 0, 3) followed by mtd_write(dev, [0x11, 0x22, 0x33], 0, 3) must leave [0x0E, 0x08, 0x00] in the page, not [0x11, 0x22, 0x33]. A write must also respect the page boundary and not write into the next page. Today a second write can set bits from 0 to 1, so the test fails.

verification.reason: The problem statement clearly describes both required behaviors (bitwise AND for re-programming, with a concrete example; and page-boundary respect for writes) and the bug (second write can set bits from 0 to 1). The hidden test checks exactly these behaviors, and the names it uses (mtd_write, mtd_emulated_dev0, mtd_dev_t) are all already present in the repository. No additional information is needed.
